title: release-verify observes the returned source checkout

design.summary:
Run release-verify's recorded consumer checks in a script-made clean copy of exactly the tree the completed return receipt records, not in the work area and not in the user's checkout.

WHEN: only at release-verify (the stage whose done_when is "observed where consumers use it"). system-test stays in the work area, because it observes the pre-release candidate.

WHERE: shiploop_workspace gains a read-only `returned_result(workspace_root)` and an `export_returned_result(workspace_root, destination)`.
- Export recipe: `git read-tree <tree>` into a private index inside the workspace root, then `git checkout-index -a -f --prefix=<dest>/`, run from the execution worktree (it shares the object database with the source), so no repository is written.
- The tree comes from the receipt's `expected_source`: `tree` for fast-forward-merge, `working_tree` for working-tree-return and no-change-return.
- The copy is `<workspace root>/consumer-check`. It is replaced on each attempt and kept after a refusal, so the model can reproduce there.
- `shiploop_test_loop.verify` runs each command with cwd set to the copy and `GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES` set to the workspace root, so a parent repository is not discovered. It records `cwd` and an optional `observed` key. `rerun_lines` and the refusal header print the same location phrase from one function.

NO COMPLETED RETURN: `workspace return` is allowed only at active release or handoff (shiploop_protocol, `workspace` return branch), so release-verify can run before the return and cannot make it. A refusal there would leave only `replan` as an exit, and would be wrong for flows that deploy from the work area and return at handoff. Behaviour is therefore unchanged: run in the work area, with no refusal. The packet and the record (`observed.where = "work-area"`, with a reason) say plainly that the checks did not observe the user's checkout, and the handoff duty reports it. In-place runs are unchanged (`observed.where = "in-place"`).

SAFETY: the user's real tree is rejected.
- For a fast-forward return, `_source_result_matches` demands an empty `git status --porcelain=v1 --untracked-files=all` in the source.
- Any file a check writes there, such as `__pycache__`, a log or a coverage directory, makes the receipt non-current, and `follow_up_knowledge_return` / `execute_return` then refuse the source as drifted.
- That strands the run at handoff with no ShipLoop route, and the lifecycle forbids deleting the user's files to clear it. Pollution of the work area, by contrast, has a route: plan-return and exclude it.
- The copy touches no repository (a scratch probe confirmed the source's index, object database and status were byte-identical afterwards), contains no ignored files such as `.env`, and is never committed.

REFUSAL TEXT (only when the run was in the returned-result copy): the header says "ran the N listed commands in a clean copy of the result returned to <source>". A paragraph then gives:
- the copy's location;
- the three usual causes: a path the return plan excluded, an ignored or unmanaged file (installed dependencies, build output), or a commit after the return (stated as a fact when the work area is ahead);
- that this stage cannot edit the commands or return;
- the exit: report `replan` with one corrective work item, so release returns the fix and release-verify observes it. If the cause is not about what was delivered (a busy port), fix it and submit done again.

CUT from the literal B3 (documented limits): the user's tree; refusing when no receipt exists; a re-observation at handoff (a possible B3b); a per-check "work-area" marker (add it, on the pattern of B2's `host_dependent`, only if a live dependency-bearing run shows false refusals); a diagnostic second run in the work area; requiring the return at release; allowing return at release-verify.
design.for_against:
FOR
- Stage and proof disagree. shiploop_stage_spec's release-verify row says "the consumer behaviour is observed where consumers use it", but `shiploop_test_loop.verify` runs the commands with cwd `state["repo"]`, which is the worktree. All four recorded release-verify test records have `cwd` ending `/worktree`: v1200-hello-sonnet, v1220-battleship-sonnet, v1220-battleship-grok-medium-none and v1230-battleship-sonnet.
- The model patches the gap by hand. In 3 of 3 recent completed runs the return was made at `release`, so release-verify ran after it. Each model then observed the returned checkout itself.
  - v1230 Sonnet's release-verify result: "Consumer observation in the delivered source directory (not the worktree) ... ShipLoop reruns the recorded consumer checks."
  - v1220 Grok's result: "ShipLoop reruns the recorded check from the worktree on this done."
  - A hand observation is not S-9 evidence.
- Older runs show the same pull, and why it is unsafe. 5 of 10 recorded runs with a receipt wrote an absolute source path into `consumer_checks` (hello, seat-reservations, v1190 x2, v1200). In v1200-hello-sonnet that command (`cd <source>/work && ... python3 -m unittest test_hello`) was the script's rerun, so it already ran in the user's real tree. Nothing broke there, but this machine sets PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1, so the run cannot show Python pollution.
- It is the only detector for a return-review misclassification: a file the product needs that the plan excluded, or an ignored file. Today every gate is green and the user holds a broken product.
- It also stops the script's own checks writing into the work area after the return. That changes the candidate fingerprint (`_candidate_matches_snapshot` compares the untracked list) and stales the receipt.
- It is small: no new state key, one mechanism reused by the packet, the verify record and the refusal, and the git recipe is proven read-only.

AGAINST
- Nothing broke in a normal run: 10 of 10 recorded receipts are fast-forward from a clean empty start, where the work area and the source hold identical tracked content.
- It adds a false-refusal class: checks that rely on unmanaged files (installed dependencies, build output, `.env`, git history). The cost of a false refusal is an outer replan. The recorded Battleship and hello products are zero-dependency, so the frequency is unknown.
- It departs from the owner's literal wording ("the returned source checkout"): the check runs in a copy of it. The owner must confirm that reading.
- No recorded run covers a working-tree-return (dirty start), so that kind is validated by hermetic real-git tests only.
- The no-return case stays unobserved and is only labelled.
- More packet text, a new Git export function to maintain, and four prompt edits.

REJECTED ALTERNATIVES
- The user's real tree: unsafe, as above. ShipLoop also runs these commands "outside the host's permission prompts" (SKILL.md), unprompted and up to 7 times.
- Allow return at release-verify: changes the `release`/`handoff` return gate in shiploop_protocol and the lifecycle invariants, for a case 3 of 3 runs avoided.
- Refuse done when no receipt: a dead end, because the stage cannot return.
- Run in the work area after checking that it equals the receipt: cannot catch an excluded or untracked file the check needs.

Verdict: implement-smaller. This is a ~70-line Git export, ~60 lines in test_loop, four prompt lines, docs and about 10 tests, all with fail-first coverage. The false-refusal unknown is bounded by the existing replan exit and the packet text. A live dependency-bearing probe before release is the owner's call.

changes.change: Resolve the workspace root, read `_manifest` and `_receipt`. Return None unless the receipt exists and has status "returned" (a missing file is None, an unreadable record raises WorkspaceError). Otherwise return {kind, tree, head, source, receipt, plan, ahead}. `tree` is receipt['expected_source']['tree'] for fast-forward-merge and ['working_tree'] for working-tree-return and no-change-return. `head` is receipt['candidate_fingerprint']['head']. `ahead` is true when `_head(worktree)` differs from it. Add to `__all__`. It does not call completed_receipt_snapshot: that compares the whole candidate fingerprint, including untracked files, so the outcome.md the model writes before `complete` at release-verify would make it report not-current.

Materialize returned_result()['tree'] into `destination`. It must be a not-yet-existing directory whose parent is the workspace root, or the call raises WorkspaceError. Use a private temp index in the workspace root (as `_temporary_index` does). Run `_git(worktree, 'read-tree', tree, env={'GIT_INDEX_FILE': idx}, readonly=True)`, then `_git(worktree, 'checkout-index', '-a', '-f', '--prefix', str(destination) + '/', env=..., readonly=True)`. Remove the index in a finally. Never `git archive`: it honours export-ignore and export-subst. No `.git` in the copy. Writes nothing to any repository: the scratch probe left the source's .git/index, object directory and status byte-identical, and preserved modes and symlinks.

changes.change: observation(root, state, stage) returns None for any stage but release-verify. Otherwise it returns {where:'in-place'} when execution_mode is not navigator-worktree (hand-built test states have no key, so they stay in-place). For a worktree run it calls workspace.returned_result(Path(root).parent) (import inside the function, as navigator._workspace_return_projection does). A result gives {where:'returned-result', kind, tree, head, source, receipt, plan, ahead}. None gives {where:'work-area', reason:'no completed return is recorded'}. One helper builds the phrase 'a clean copy of the result returned to <source> (<kind> at <head12>; receipt <path>)' or 'the work area <repo>', used by both rerun_lines and verify's refusal header (S-12). Add to `__all__`.

After the `refused >= MAX_REFUSED_RUNS` early return and before `deadline` is computed, call observation(). For returned-result: replace <workspace root>/consumer-check, call export_returned_result, run every command (and nothing else at this stage) with cwd set to the copy and env GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES=<workspace root>. A WorkspaceError during export makes every command row status 'error' with the message as stderr (disposition could-not-run, an existing exit; it does not count toward the 7). The record keeps `cwd` = where the commands really ran and adds the optional `observed` mapping (release-verify only). The refusal header becomes 'ran the N listed commands in <phrase>'. When where is returned-result, append the paragraph: the copy's location; the three causes (excluded by the return plan, ignored or unmanaged file, commit after the return, the last as a fact when ahead is true); that this stage cannot edit the commands or return; the exit 'report outcome replan with one corrective work item so release returns the fix and release-verify observes it'; and 'if the cause is not about what was delivered (a busy port), fix it and submit done again'. That paragraph replaces the generic 'Fix the code ... submit done again' tail for this case only. Other stages and the work-area and in-place cases are untouched.

New required `root` parameter. For release-verify it prints the phrase: 'Test rerun: on done, ShipLoop runs every test command release-plan recorded from <phrase> and refuses unless each passes ...'. The work-area variant adds: no completed return is recorded, so these commands do not observe the user's checkout; a return is allowed at release and handoff; return at release to have them observe it. 'recorded from' is kept in every variant, so the existing pins hold.
Pass `root` to test_loop.rerun_lines in the RERUN_STAGES branch. This is the only caller outside tests.

release-plan, in the consumer_checks paragraph: when a return is recorded before release-verify the checks run in a clean copy of it, otherwise in the work area and ShipLoop says so; write paths relative to the checkout, put what a fresh consumer needs (install, build) into the check itself, and do not write into the user's checkout by absolute path. release: in an isolated run, make the source return here when release-verify's checks should observe the delivered result. release-verify: state the copy semantics and that a defect is fixed through replan because this stage cannot return; anything run inside the user's checkout must leave it exactly as the return left it (a written file stales the receipt and blocks handoff). handoff: say where release-verify's checks ran (the record's `observed`); a work-area run did not observe the returned checkout. Every packet restates its own part (S-6).

'On done, ShipLoop runs every consumer check release-plan recorded, in a copy of the returned result when a return is recorded.' (printed under Considerations; check test/shiploop-stage-spec.test.py for a pin).

Add a short subsection: which checkout release-verify observes, with the three cases (copy of the returned result, work area with a label, in-place), why the user's tree is not used (strict clean-status receipt; no ShipLoop route out of a polluted source), and the limits: no Git history in the copy, a command that names the checkout by absolute path runs there, unmanaged files are absent.

unknowns: Frequency of false refusals from checks that depend on unmanaged files (installed dependencies, build output, .env, git history). Recorded consumer checks are zero-dependency Python or Node, or use absolute source paths, so there is no evidence either way. How settled: (a) the hermetic fixture proves the refusal text and the replan exit; (b) a read-only replay script over the 10 recorded runs with a receipt (export each returned tree, rerun the recorded consumer_checks; the 5 absolute-path ones are unaffected by cwd); (c) a live dependency-bearing case (npm or pip), which cannot be achieved now because no E2E case has dependencies. Owner decision: whether (c) gates the release. Trigger for the per-check work-area marker: one false refusal in (b) or (c), not before.

Working-tree-return and no-change-return have never occurred in any recorded run (10 of 10 receipts are fast-forward from a clean start). Validated another way: hermetic real-git fixtures for all three kinds. Not achievable live until an E2E case starts from a dirty source.

Whether models will keep observing by hand inside the user's checkout and leave files there (the guidance asks them not to). Settled by the live Sonnet run: after release-verify, `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all` in the source must be empty and handoff must complete; the handoff guard (`completed_receipt`) already refuses otherwise.

Export time and disk on a large repository (unmeasured). The export runs before the stage budget clock starts and is bounded by `_git_timeout()`. Settled by a one-off timing on this repository and a recorded number in the journal; unmeasured stays unknown.

Whether the receipt's `working_tree` tree objects survive git gc. They are unreferenced objects written by write-tree, but completed_receipt_snapshot and _fingerprint_matches_snapshot already read the same ids, so no new dependency; a pruned object would show as could-not-run.
GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES semantics across git versions: the probe on this machine showed git stops at the ceiling and finds a parent repo without it. Settled by the parent-repository test.

Packet-bounds: the release-verify packet grows by about 2 lines in one block. Settled by running shiploop-packet-bounds and shiploop-delegation (raise a bound, never trim, per the owner's memory rule).
Whether the Run Review session wants to show `observed` on the stage card. The keys are additive and optional. Hand-off note only; nothing is planned under skills/shiploop-run-review.

Owner decisions the plan needs: (1) accept 'a clean copy of the returned result' as the reading of 'the returned source checkout'; (2) accept label-only (no refusal, no handoff re-run) when release-verify precedes the return; (3) whether a handoff re-observation (B3b) is wanted later. It would add handoff to the rerun stages when the release-verify record says work-area, a second change of B3's size touching stage_spec complete_runs, RERUN_STAGES, packets and the remedy tests.
risks: SPEC change admission, S-6 (packets stand alone): mitigated. The release-verify packet states where the commands run, how they are checked, and the exit; the where-text is regenerated at every `next`. Tested by the packet test.

S-9 / the proof: the returned-result case is strengthened. The no-return case stays work-area and is labelled in the packet and the record, with the handoff duty to report it. Accepted: the lifecycle forbids returning at release-verify and allows deferring the return to handoff.

Break another style, host, language or platform (checks that rely on unmanaged files, git history or absolute paths): accepted with mitigation. The refusal names the causes and the replan exit, and the release-plan duty tells the author to bring what a fresh consumer needs. A command that names the checkout by absolute path ignores the copy, as 5 of 10 recorded runs did; this is pre-existing and documented, because blocking the path would also block read-only checks such as the seat-reservations `git -C <source> cat-file -e HEAD:server.py`. Live frequency is unknown (see unknowns).

Fail silently or pass tests while failing live: the three return kinds are covered by real-git tests. Only the fast-forward kind has a live run (the Sonnet Battleship rerun on the build); the other two have none and the journal must say so.

Model-written glue, host refusals, recovery dead ends, waiting on a person (S-14): no new glue. The refusal's exit is `replan`, which release-verify already accepts (existing all-stage remedy test). An export failure is could-not-run, an existing exit. The no-return case never refuses, which avoids a dead end. Nothing waits on a person.
Enlarge packet text or context: about 2 lines in one packet, plus four DUTIES sentences. Repetition across packets is the tenet; nothing is repeated inside one packet.

Leak or commit secrets, touch user work outside the run, change the user's repository or history: mitigated. Export reads Git objects only and runs from the execution worktree; the probe showed the source index, objects and status unchanged; ignored files such as .env are not in the copy; the copy lives in the workspace root outside the product and the run records, and is never in a return plan. Rejected variant, the user's tree: an untracked file or log stales the receipt and blocks handoff with no ShipLoop exit (existing test test_knowledge_follow_up_refuses_a_moved_source shows the refusal), and destructive recorded commands would run unprompted on the real tree. No cleanup is automatic (workspace-lifecycle: no automatic cleanup), so one product copy remains per workspace until the user removes it.

Break saved runs, callers, tests, adapters, catalogs: no state key is added (strict keys untouched), `observed` is an optional key in test-loop verify records that only test_loop reads, and no old-format path is added. The only signature change is rerun_lines(root, ...): one production caller (navigator.render) and two tests. An in-flight run paused at release-verify with a recorded return starts using the copy on resume. Run Review does not read verify records (grep of skills/shiploop-run-review/scripts found no use).

Cost more than it saves: one export plus one rerun per release-verify attempt (up to 7), against a stage the 2026-10-07 Sonnet run recorded as short. The saving is the model's by-hand observations, which are still allowed, so the gain is evidence quality, not turns. Unmeasured.

Gamed: a model can record `consumer_checks_na`, or an absolute-path command that bypasses the copy. Both exist today and are visible in the recorded result, which the release-plan Improve review reads. Not adversarially hardened (KISS).

Other stages: system-test and the INNER stages call the same verify() but observation() returns None for them, so nothing changes. consumer-delivery `behavior` obligations at release-verify are model-recorded evidence and are unaffected (run shiploop-consumer-delivery to confirm).

Interaction with a product fix found at release-verify: previously the model could fix it in the work area and finish, with the handoff follow-up return delivering the fix unobserved. Now the copy (the delivered tree) still fails, so the route is replan, which re-runs the outer stages and returns again. This is slower but is the honest flow; the refusal states `ahead` when it applies. Accepted.

A check that passes in the work area but fails on what was delivered, for example because the return plan excluded a file it needs, is refused with the location, the usual causes and the one exit the stage has (`replan`). When no return has been made yet, the checks run in the work area exactly as before and the packet, the test record (`observed`) and the handoff say so; the run is not refused. In-place runs are unchanged. The `release-plan`, `release`, `release-verify` and `handoff` duties, SKILL.md and the workspace lifecycle card say where the checks run and ask for relative paths, checks that bring what a fresh consumer needs, and no writes into the user's checkout. What happens at replan from a copy refusal: the corrective item runs the full inner loop plus the outer stages. This is the existing remedy pattern, but its cost for a one-line check change (add an install) is unmeasured.

title: script-completed skill-assess and skill-validate when not applicable

design.summary:
Build B6 smaller than the plan wrote it. The step plan opts out explicitly with a new optional key, `skill_na` (the reason no repo-local skill is selected, created or changed for the item). The script then records skill-assess and skill-validate as "Not applicable to this item" in the ledger, with no packet and no model turn. The skill-surface list does not go in as a path class. Reasons:
- A class before `docs` and listed non-behavioural would make `skills/x/scripts/run.py` (code today) skip the test stages.
- A class before `docs` and not listed non-behavioural would make `skills/x/SKILL.md` (docs today) start requiring them.
- So the surface is a separate top-level `skill_surface` list in `references/path-classes.json`, read by one new function. `classify`, `behavioural`, `order` and `non_behavioural` do not read it.

The proof is state-only, the exact twin of `item_scope.no_test_item`:
1. The latest accepted done step plan for the item carries `skill_na`.
2. No declared path is, or could name, a skill-surface file (`SKILL.md`, `skills/` or `agents/` trees, the host agent-config dirs, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, `.mcp.json`; the knowledge home `docs/shiploop/` is exempt; wildcard directories count as possibly skill).

`navigator.apply` stays pure. The existing `_record_not_applicable_tests` loop becomes one `_record_not_applicable` loop over test and skill stages. Anything short of the proof issues both stages exactly as today. That is the base path, not a fallback. No state key is added and nothing is migrated.

Two cheaper designs were rejected:
- Observation-only (no declaration; script-complete when the repo holds no skill file and the diff touches none) needs an impure transition inside `complete`. It would also change every CLI-driven walk through a no-skill temp repo (full-runtime, consumer-delivery, callback-contract).
- A refusal gate on the diff at `document`, mirroring `scope_refusal`, is an optional second increment (see risks).
design.for_against:
FOR:
- 44 of 44 skill-assess and skill-validate visits (22 item visits in 17 run ledgers under /Users/dadleet/e2e-runs, five products: hello, seat-reservations, Node Battleship, battleship-scoring, Google Apps Script Battleship) ended done with a no-skill or N/A disposition. None cites a skill-surface file in evidence_refs. No product worktree holds SKILL.md, AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md. This is wider than the "one product" evidence behind the deferral.
- The decision is already made twice before skill-assess: discovery records fit or no-fit with locators, and step-plan must reopen the index (`shiploop_prompts.DUTIES` "discovery" and "step-plan"). In the Grok 20261007 run the step plan's plan.md already said "No repo skill applies", and skill-assess then re-wrote a "Skill disposition" section plus a knowledge commit ("after skill-assess", worktree commit 07d1829).
- Measured cost per item in the four runs: 16, 51, 68, 8, 48 and 50 s (mean 40 s), 2 to 7 turns per stage, 0.76% to 1.96% of summed stage seconds per run (metrics.json). Luna 1.16.1 spent 5.8 min on one item (3.8 + 2.0). Each stage packet is 27 to 37 KB (evidence JSONs).
- Mechanical work belongs to the script (SPEC S-5). The proof is state-only, so `apply` stays pure and the work reuses one mechanism (S-12).
- Failure is safe. A missing or wrong declaration only means the model stages run as today.
- The positive case (a repo that has skills, the 2026-09-18 local-skills pilot) is untouched. Its fixture has no `skill_na`, and `test/experiments/shiploop_local_skills/test_packet_routes.py` still renders both packets.

AGAINST:
- The gain is small, at most about 2% of stage time and 2 to 19 turns per run. Token cost per stage is unmeasured (metrics.json stages carry seconds, turns and tool_calls only).
- It adds an optional key to the busiest packet (step-plan), which B7 and B12 also edit.
- Adoption is unproven. The Sonnet 20261007 step plan recorded no skill rationale at all, though the prompt asks for one, so prose-only opt-in may be skipped. The cost of skipping is the status quo.
- Every harness case is a small one-off app with no skill index, so 44 of 44 is selection-biased and shows nothing about skill-rich repos.
- Opting out removes the third nudge to create a skill in a no-skill repo. 0 of 44 visits created one.
- An undeclared skill edit after step-plan is not detected at skill time. It is never committed (`item_scope.commit_item` leaves undeclared paths and names them), but it is also not validated.

Verdict: implement-smaller. It is the lowest-priority item of the batch; drop it first if time is short, with no loss to correctness.

design.summary: Add a record-only `planning` block to the harness `metrics.json`, written by `test/shiploop_e2e/metrics.py` (and `rollouts.py` for Codex). It holds: the planning window on two labelled clocks (engine and host); per-stage seconds with the Improve share split out; plan shape as counts only; and output/reasoning tokens where the host's per-call counts are proven exact (Grok, Codex). It replaces the 11-agent ledger evaluation for its primary tiling and its token ledger. I ran the readers as scratch prototypes on six real run directories. They reproduced the earlier account's numbers: Luna xhigh window 374.95 min, Improve 203.35, other 171.6, per-stage Improve 44.5/61.1/56.9/26.7/14.2; Grok `none` 20.5 engine / 22.05 host; Grok 86,986 output tokens at 43% reasoning; Luna 1,153,899 output at 59%. Separately, make the engine's existing planning clock record-only: in the preparation scope the narrative Pace row keeps "N steps in X min" and drops the "about N min left" forecast, which was 3 to 6 times short early in 4 of 4 recorded runs. Not proposed: a row in the status block, anything in the context index, per-stage tokens, the class cut or Backchain split of the ledger, a baseline-row key, or any exporter edit. The reasons are in for_against and unknowns.
design.for_against:
FOR. (1) The numbers are small pure functions over records the run already keeps. `state.md` history is joined to `timeline.json` (`metrics.stage_results`, `metrics.acceptance_stamps`). The engine's own `state["improve_results"]` keys equal the `improve/<action>-bind.md` files in all six real runs, so "a child ran" has an authority. The step plan's `steps` with `deps` is validated by `shiploop_navigator._normalise_steps`. A ~60-line scratch reader matched the account's primary tiling and token ledger, so the 11-agent workflow is not needed for them. (2) The definition clashes recorded in `docs/pending-work-plan-2026-10-06.md` and README go away: 72.7 vs 72.0 vs 71.88, 42.4 vs 45.9 vs 45.82, and the engine vs host clock (20.5 vs 22.05; 374.95 vs 375.93). One function labels both clocks. (3) Work-item count alone, the dropped B9 idea, misleads: items/steps are Sonnet (1 item, 5 steps in 1.23.0; 1 item, 3 steps in 1.22.0) against Grok (2 items, 1 step each, both releases). The step list, with its deps, is the executable-step measure. (4) The preparation forecast is plainly misleading. After step 5 Grok forecast "3 min left" with 10.3 actual; after step 2 it forecast 6 against 14.4 actual; Sonnet forecast 1 against 4.4 actual. Cause: preparation stages differ in size by about 40 times (intake 0.2 min, plan 9.5 min on Grok). The work-items and release forecasts were within roughly 30% on the runs I checked, so I leave them alone. S-15 itself says "observed pace". (5) No state key and no change to a saved run: the harness block is derived, and the narrative change only sets an existing field to 0.

AGAINST. (a) Counts cannot say "too few" or "too many" without outcome data. n is 4 plans on one case, and no threshold is invented. The block makes the owner's check cheap but does not make the judgement. (b) Improve seconds use file times of `improve/<action>-bind.md`. They are right only on the original run directory: the run-doc figures 72.0/45.9/26.1 differ from the original directories (71.88/45.82/26.06), plausibly because the run docs were made from copies. (c) It is a third implementation of stage minutes beside `export.py` (bind to receipt) and the harness stage rows, unless the Run Review session's C2 reads `metrics.json` `planning`. That is a handoff, not my edit. (d) The narrative change alters a documented, tested display (`status-display.md`; `test_pace_needs_two_steps_and_labels_the_estimate` pins the formatter, not the facts). The owner may prefer a better forecast to none. (e) A status-block row is rejected. `status_block(state)` is a pure function of state, pinned by `test/shiploop-navigator-contract.test.py`, and it would need the timeline as well. `status.md` is rewritten only on transitions, so a "so far" figure would be stale. The Claude hook's `shiploop_status_hook.compact` prints only Where/Done/Waiting/Stopped/Next, so the row would never reach a CLI user. The packet embeds the block, so the model would see it, though it already sees Pace. (f) The context index is rejected: it is a model-read pointer file, and no stage needs a measure (main tenet).

VERDICT implement-smaller. Build the harness block (counts and durations only, nothing gating), the harness summary and progress lines, and the preparation-pace change. Leave the rest.

changes.change: `collect` adds a top-level `planning` key built from the already-read `state`, `accepted` rows (`stage_results` carries each row's action id) and `stamps`. `window`: `seconds` is the engine clock, from `timeline.json` `started` to the first accepted `test-spec` with outcome done. `host_seconds` is the same end minus `min(stamps)`, the rule `stage_windows` uses. `before_engine_seconds` is the difference. `closed` is true or false. An open window reports `through` (the last stamped stage) and never 0. One unstamped row inside the window, or a first planning accept before the host's first event (a harness-seeded run), gives `{"unmeasured": reason}`, never a shorter number. `rows`: per accepted visit in the window `{stage, workitem, outcome, seconds, improve_seconds}`. `improve_seconds` is the accept stamp minus the mtime of `improve/<action>-bind.md` when `action in state["improve_results"]`, measured 0 when it is not, and null with a reason when the result exists but the bind file is missing or `improve_results` is absent. `improve` totals children and seconds. `producer_seconds` is the window minus Improve. `preparation_seconds` ends at the `prepare` accept, so it matches the narrative's Preparation scope. `shape` is counts only, from `planning_revision.current_actions(state)` (the engine's own latest-done-step-plan rule, which already handles revise and reconcile): `items_planned` (the accepted plan result's `work_items`), `items_now` (`state["work_items"]`), and per item `steps`, `roots` (deps []), `groups` (longest dependency chain, the same layering as the Backchain check's `parallel_groups`), `widest_group`, `paths`, `criteria`, and `planning_seconds` (that item's step-plan plus test-spec visits). An item with no accepted step plan gets null counts and `planned: false`. A step plan with a step lacking the `deps` key gets `steps` but null graph figures with the reason, since `_normalise_steps` preserves omission and 'missing dependencies do not mean independent steps'. Totals are null when any part is unknown. `tokens` is {output, reasoning, source}, or {unmeasured: reason}. For Grok it sums `usage` events' `output_tokens` and `reasoning_tokens` over the window; `collect` keeps a `(t, output, reasoning)` list beside `turns`. For Codex it calls `rollouts.rollout_tokens`. Claude is unmeasured, with its streaming-snapshot reason. Reasons live inside the block. The top-level `unmeasured` map is NOT touched, because four tests pin its exact key sets. `summary_lines` inserts one `planning ...` line before the costliest-stages line (tests index `[0]` and `[-1]`), guarded by `metrics.get("planning")`. `per_stage`, `stage_windows`, `baseline_stages` and `improve_reviews` are unchanged. Docstring states that `improve_seconds` is bind to accept, so the tiles sum to the window, and that `improve_reviews.seconds` is a different quantity.

`_read` keeps `output_tokens` and `reasoning_output_tokens` from each `token_usage_record`'s `usage`. `rollout_tokens(out, start, end)` sums main-thread records with start < t <= end, deduped by `response_id`, and reports sub-agent output beside the main figure instead of inside it. It returns `{unmeasured: reason}` when there are no rollouts or no call (reusing `NO_ROLLOUTS`, `NO_CALLS`). The window is read in the same pass as `rollout_context`, so there is no second read of the 225 MB files. Module docstring gains the verified fact that per-call sums equal the thread's cumulative `thread_token_usage` on all 5 threads of the Luna 1.21.0 run.

When the planning window is closed and not yet reported, print one line (window on both clocks, Improve share, items and steps). Add a `planning` key to the `.progress.json` memo so it prints once. This is the live record-only planning clock for the E2E watcher, with no engine change.

title: resume and retry class: exact run-dir and next command everywhere, long-run pinning

design.summary: Packets and the engine already print the exact run-dir and next command at every stage, so no skills/shiploop change is warranted. Printing more cannot fix the Luna path mangling. The real gaps are all in the E2E harness (test/shiploop_e2e), and a later step would settle only the Codex pin. (1) The harness resume prompt names a bare `shiploop next` for a Claude run built from a checkout. (2) A deliberate stop, or a killed harness, leaves no metrics.json, result.json or review export, and a killed host is relaunched. (3) The README's description of the background-task limit is stale. Recommended: a resume prompt that names the CLI the run actually uses (bare fallback deleted), a clean stop (`--stop-at STAGE` plus an `<out>/stop` file) that flows through the normal finalization, `--grade-only` for a run whose harness is gone, a printed exact resume command, and corrected docs with a characterization test for the `--timeout` recipe. Drop packet and engine changes, typo prevention, a signal handler and a stage-boundary time budget. The Codex pin is investigation-only.
design.for_against:
FOR. Packets and engine (verified in code and in the saved runs): `shiploop_navigator.packet_head` prints the exact callback (`--run-dir=`), `Recovery (reprints this head and rewrites the full packet)`, `Pause` and the keepalive marker with `dir=`. `_run_rules` writes `Recovery command:` into every packet file; all 47 files in v1230-battleship-sonnet and all 50 in v1230-battleship-grok-none carry it. Blocked and paused packets print `Resume:` (`render`), and the awaiting route prints `resume --answer/--observed`. Halted prints nothing, which is correct. The product driver already takes the command from `hook-status` (`shiploop_protocol.hook_status`, `shiploop_keepalive._driver_prompt`), so the product side follows S-1/S-4.

Resume prompt, measured. The four Luna resume prompts (`resume-codex-*.txt`) were exact, yet the first `next` command had a mangled run-dir in 3 of 4 resumed sessions. The mangles were a duplicated `20261005/` segment (events 592, exit 2), a dropped `v` (event 1210, exit 2) and an inserted `./` (event 2631, resolved by luck). Grok's two resumes were exact. Each failed attempt was repaired by the very next call, about 10 s. The 1003 reopen rule R2 (a typo not repaired by the next call, or a run blocked by one) is not met.

Re-orientation is not an address problem. In 6 of 6 resumes the first `next` ran within 8 to 18 s and the packet was read within 35 to 100 s. Luna's first `complete` came 948 to 1868 s after the resume because the kills fell inside Improve passes of 22 to 34 min whose work was redone. The ledger's "orientation 10.8, 13.4, 1.1, 18.2 min per kill" is that replay, not run-finding.

Verified gap 1: `resume_prompt` falls back to a bare `shiploop next` when `Host.plugin_cli` finds nothing. `ClaudeHost.plugin_cli` looks only under `<out>/marketplace`, so a Claude `--source checkout` run (v1220 and v1230 Sonnet) gets the bare command. I computed this on the real v1230 folder. It is the defect 7c1f1014 fixed for the marketplace route (13 turns lost). A test pins the bare command as intended, `test_without_an_installed_marketplace_build_the_bare_command_remains`. `seed_run`'s call site already uses the right rule, `host.plugin_cli(out/"home") or plugin_dir/skills/shiploop/scripts/shiploop`.

Verified gap 2: all 3 deliberate stops since 2026-10-04 left no records. They were v1200-battleship-luna (stopped after about 48 min per docs/shiploop-run-review-journal.md), v1210-battleship-grok-medium (a planning-only probe) and v1210-battleship-luna-xhigh (the owner stopped it at 588 min). None has result.json, metrics.json or review-export, while the 7 runs that ended on their own all have them. A host kill is relaunched by the `host.resumable` loop in `main`. The 2026-09-27 temperature-report run was "killed deliberately to stop a resume loop". The Grok probe's ad hoc auto-stop overshot into test-author (LEARNINGS, 2026-10-05 corrections). The audit harness already has this idea (`--stop-after-stage`, outcome `done`, `accepted_after_boundary`, `stopped-at-observed-boundary`), so the vocabulary and rule have prior art.

Verified gap 3: the README says a task is killed after "18-30 minutes". The measured limit is about 7200 s (relaunch gaps of 7208, 7208 and 7211 s between consecutive Luna resumes). The default `--timeout` is 10800, above the limit. A `--timeout` below the limit already ends through the existing deadline path and finalizes (`launch` returns `timeout`, the resume loop stops with "run deadline spent", then metrics, result and export are written). That needs documenting and a characterization test, not code. The regrade-a-blocked-run commit 977b238b is the template for `--grade-only`.

Cost. Polling `grade_shiploop` costs 10 to 30 ms on the largest run folder (259 MB, 5,490 files), so a 2 s poll is cheap. No engine state key changes.

AGAINST and dropped. Engine and packet changes, such as a run-dir inferred from the cwd or an env fallback, are not justified. Typing cost is seconds, the lever (a zero-retype command) is a new ShipLoop verb, and the 1003 decision deferred the same class. Having the harness pre-run `next` and paste the head into the prompt would stop the host session from binding the keepalive marker. A SIGTERM handler is unproven, because what the task runner sends is unknown, so the stop file is the deterministic route. A soft stage-boundary time budget would avoid about 43 min of kill replay in the one 10-hour Luna run (n=1), but it needs two interacting numbers. It is a candidate for the next planned Codex run, not part of this change. The Codex pin (`marketplace add --ref <sha>`) is unproven and the existing refusal (a0925b33) plus not releasing during a live Codex run covers the exposure, so it is investigation-only.

changes.symbol: resume_prompt, new run_cli(host_name, out, plugin_dir), main (resumed opening, post-interrupt argv, resume-loop argv), seed_run call site
changes.change: `resume_prompt(run_dir, cli)` always names `python3 "<cli>" next --run-dir "<run_dir>"`. The bare `shiploop next` branch is deleted. One helper `run_cli(host_name, out, plugin_dir)` returns `hosts.host(host_name).plugin_cli(out/"home") or plugin_dir/"skills/shiploop/scripts/shiploop"`, the expression `seed_run`'s caller already uses. It is used for the first resume (`earlier['host']`, `earlier['plugin_dir']`, so a cross-host resume keeps the original run's CLI), the post-interrupt resume and the resume loop. `main` raises SystemExit naming the missing CLI before any host starts when a non-regrade resume finds the file gone; a regrade never needs it.

Add `--stop-at STAGE` (choices `shiploop_stage_spec.STAGES`; reached when `metrics.engine_state(run_dir)['history']` has an entry with that stage and outcome `done`, the audit harness's rule; first accept only; run located with `grade_shiploop(out)` each poll). Add a `<out>/stop` file: any process may create it; it is consumed (unlinked) when acted on and cleared at the start of every invocation. One `StopRequest` object is polled as `launch`'s `stop_when` and checked before each relaunch in the resume loop. `launch` takes `stop_status` (default `interrupted` so the chain test is unchanged; `stopped` for a request) or returns the string the predicate gave. The predicate swallows read errors and returns False. On a stop: no relaunch, no interrupt-recovery, no product checks (`check_results` empty), no baseline row (the 'a resumed or seeded run is not a baseline' line gains 'a stopped run'), no mismatch.md, `process['pass']` is None (a requested stop is not a failed host), exit code 0, header `STOPPED` instead of `FAIL`. Metrics, result.json and `review_export(out)` run as for any run. Refused: `--stop-at` with `--suite` or `--interrupt-at`, `--stop-at` on a done or blocked resume, and a stage already accepted when a resume starts (the message names the engine's last stage and says to pick a later one).

A stop records `process_status: stopped`, `resume_stop: 'stopped after <stage> (--stop-at)'` or `'stopped by <out>/stop'`, and an optional `stop_overshoot` (history entries accepted after the requested one, 0 normally; the Grok probe's overshoot becomes visible). The printed `stopped` line shows the overshoot when above 0. All new keys are optional; nothing else is required.

`--grade-only` is valid only with `--resume-run`. It extends the existing regrade path: `regrade = status in ('done','blocked') or (args.grade_only and status is not None)`. No host starts; the recorded host, model, effort and plugin verdict are restated; metrics.json, result.json and the review export are written from what is on disk. This covers a run whose harness was killed (2 h limit, an owner kill) and whose records were never written. A paused or halted run is no longer refused under this flag. A blocked run is never continued, per S-14.

Print once at start (before any host spend) and again at the end whenever the engine is still active: `resume: python3 <run.py> --resume-run <out> --host <h> --model <m> --effort <e>` with the recorded values. Any later session reading the task log, even after a SIGKILL of the harness, then holds the exact output dir and command.

title: script-owned document checks instead of model-written check scripts

design.summary: Build no new document checker. Measured, the lever is mostly not document checks: in the Luna xhigh 1.21.0 run (planning window 375.0 min, 196 inline scripts) the pure document checks are 22 scripts and 8.9 min. That agrees with the pending-work plan's 7.5 min, not the ledger's "100 scripts, 73.8 min, 35 to 55 savable". In the four named runs, the Grok none runs have no document-check script at all; the Sonnet stage-mode runs have 3 to 4 counts-only passes (below). The rest of Luna's scripts are Improve and Backchain loop glue (68 scripts, 44.8 min, S-5 / open item a02) and document authoring (52 scripts, 37.5 min). Every generic check that recurs is already owned and refusing: result JSON shape, evidence-file existence, assumption list and its evidence files, criterion-to-command coverage, step deps order, credential screen, dropped R-id, required knowledge files. The graph check `backchain-check` stays record-only. What does recur is a packet defect and a refusal-route defect: (P1) 23 of 34 stage packets, including spec, plan, step-plan and test-spec, say "Checked by: nothing automatic beyond the result's form", which is false for plan and step-plan and invites the model to re-implement the gates; (P2) a result file that fails to parse is refused on the "Request failure ... Do not infer a next action ... follow the recovery packet" route that was made for lost state, not as a rejected request to fix and resubmit. Build P1 and P2 only (both small, no state key, no new file kind, no compatibility path). Link/anchor/whitespace checks and R-id mention checks are not worth owning on this evidence; each has a measured re-open trigger below.
design.for_against: FOR the two small fixes. P1: the Checked-by line exists to tell a cleared model how its result is checked (main tenet, SPEC S-6, commit 44427a98), but it derives only from the stage row's complete_runs, so for 23 of 34 stages it says nothing automatic runs. Real 1.23.0 packets (g1230 run, packets/*.md) show that text on intake, discovery, research, spec, test-strategy, plan, prepare, get-next-work-item, step-plan, test-spec and others. Yet complete refuses an incomplete plan assumption list (`_check_submitted_assumptions`), a step-plan with uncovered criteria, forward deps or bad paths (`_normalise_criteria`, `_normalise_steps`, `_check_submitted_test_commands`), a missing evidence file (`_check_submitted_evidence`), a credential (`_reject_credentials`), and missing knowledge files or a dropped R-id (`shiploop_knowledge_home.check`). Models re-implement exactly these. Criteria coverage by hand: l1210, gm1210, s1230 (step-plan checks.md "criteria covered ... step deps ok: True"), g1230 (step-plan "uncovered" script). Evidence-ref existence by hand: l1210 (at least 3) and gm1210. Credential screens: gm1210 (5+). Result-JSON pre-check before complete: all six runs. P2: 3 of 16 run folders in /Users/dadleet/e2e-runs hit the heavy route on a malformed model-written result (v1190-hello-sonnet empty file, v1200-hello-sonnet three refusals, v1230 grok-none). The sibling failures in the same function, `_submitted_result`, already use the light NavigatorError route ("run the same complete command again"). The fix is about 4 lines. AGAINST building more: (1) no saving is demonstrable. The refusal in g1230 cost about 0.2 min (refusal at +17.10, next at +17.19, packet at +17.28). Document-check scripts in the Sonnet and Grok none runs cost seconds. Luna's 8.9 min is 2.4% of its window. (2) The generic checks find nothing. Of 43 Luna scripts with a markdown-link regex (24 read-only, 5.8 min, 5 distinct slug() implementations), none reported a broken link, anchor or trailing whitespace; the only gaps found were product-specific content assertions ("missing: Content-Type: application/json", "PORT unset", "missing valid fleet boundary") that a script cannot own. All six delivered knowledge homes have 0 trailing-whitespace lines and 0 broken anchors (GitHub-style slug); one has a broken relative file link (g1230 docs/shiploop/README.md links ../SHIPLOOP.md, should be ../../SHIPLOOP.md), and that run had no review pass. (3) R-id mention checks are unsafe on free prose: the strategy mentions every living-spec R-id in 6 of 6 homes (nothing to find), while the plans of s1220 ("R-1..R-9") and s1230 ("R-1..R-10", "Every R-id is owned by W1") would false-positive on range notation, and a mention is not coverage. The design doc's own limit says none of the 9 warranted findings would be caught by this class of check. (4) P1 and P2 may not change model behaviour (unknown U1); the P1 claim rests on a verifiable text-versus-code mismatch plus the observed re-implementations, not on a measured saving.

title: cheaper revise path and script-derived Improve opening

design.summary:
Build one packet-only change: a work item sent back to step-plan gets a packet that names its previous step plan and the result that sent it back, and asks the model to amend the plan and say which rows are carried over. It copies the shipped `_replan_delta_lines` precedent (navigator), needs no state key and touches no gate or protected loop. Drop the script-derived Improve opening. Drop any engine "cheaper revise" (skipped stages, delta-only review, prefilled template, fewer Improve passes). The "no real module for the tests to load" guard already shipped as the `test-probe` run at `test-author` and needs nothing.

Why only this much:
- With the two hosts on current defaults, a revise redo cost 28% and 45% of the first pass, not 3.1x.
- The one 3.1x case (Luna xhigh, 1.21.0) differs from the cheap Grok redo in one visible way. Grok amended: all 8 criteria kept verbatim, C9 added. Luna rewrote: all 4 criteria reworded, 1 step became 5, 2 test commands became 7, and the Improve review took 76.4 min against 26.7. Telling the model to amend is the only lever that touches neither the Backchain pass nor the Improve child, both protected by S-10 (the loop-until-checked rule).
- Opening files cost 0.5 to 1.7 minutes per child on current hosts, with 1 refusal in 23 children.
design.for_against:
FOR the packet change.
- Under the main tenet, the redone step-plan packet is byte-identical to the first visit's except for the revision number and the "Last accepted transition" block. I diffed the Grok packets nav-29a5... (first visit) and nav-ee2f... (redo) in the 1.23.0 run.
- The redo packet never says it is an amendment and never names the previous plan. "Results this stage builds on" lists spec, test-strategy, plan and prepare. `planning_revision.current_actions` marks the earlier step plan as superseded, and it appears only in context-index.md under "Superseded results".
- The "Last accepted transition" block holds the revise evidence only while the revise result is the last history entry. A `repeat` of the redone step-plan replaces it.
- The wording and shape are proven by `_replan_delta_lines`, which prints "This stage's result before the replan: <path>. Keep its evidence for everything these paths do not affect ... say in the summary which rows are new and which are carried over."
- It is about 25 lines of code, with no state key and no protocol bump.

AGAINST, and why it stays small.
- Nothing is broken on current defaults. Two redos are measured: Sonnet 1.22.0 redid 10 stages in 1.18 min against 4.23 for the first pass; Grok 1.23.0 redid step-plan and test-spec in 2.28 min against 5.08.
- Three of the four known revises were engine gaps since fixed:
  - the node:test counter, c38f6887;
  - the missing-module probe, e11b86ef;
  - the revise route after could-not-run, 6a59012c.
  Only the Grok path error was a genuine plan error.
- The Luna growth (result 8.0 KB to 20.5 KB, review 2.9x) is one run on another host and release. It may have been partly necessary, because the revise reason required a new "real module seam" step.
- The time effect is therefore unmeasured. I claim a tenet and recovery fix, not a time saving.
- Prompt-only, so nothing enforces the amendment. A refusal on an unchanged plan would be wrong, because a revise that originated in test-spec can leave the step plan legitimately unchanged.

DROPPED parts.
- Script-derived Improve opening.
  - Of 23 Improve children across the four runs, 1 improve-start was refused. It was the Grok 1.23.0 end-of-work child: contract 9,450 B, 234 over the 9,216 budget, fixed in about 39 s.
  - Sonnet openings were 0.9 to 1.6 KB, written in the same command as the start.
  - The expensive case is Luna xhigh: 4 refusals with 3 the size guard (LEARNINGS 927) and 26.3 min of openings over 5 children (LEARNINGS 1383).
  - The part that grows is conversation-only. The Grok end-of-work "Current learnings" (facts, decisions, hypotheses, pitfalls, events line 12285) cannot be derived from state.
  - Scope, Authority and Environment are partly derivable, and `improve_start_contract` already adds the commit policy and exclusions. But deriving them is a medium change with a wrong-scope risk and an unfixed default (pending-work-plan C5, fast-planning-plan c8/D8).
  - Under `planning_review none` a run has 2 to 3 children instead of 8 to 10.
- Engine cheaper revise. Skipping stages, reviewing only the delta, a prefilled template or fewer Improve passes would each trade S-10 rigour or save seconds. The result record is only about 1,200 tokens, which is 20 to 25 s of output at Luna's decode rate.
- Test-red guard. Nothing to add; see evidence.

changes.change: Add `_revise_delta_lines(root, state, stage, workitem)`. When `stage == stage_spec.REVISE_TO`, `workitem` is not None and `state['revisions'].get(workitem)` is truthy, it finds the item's latest history entry with outcome 'revise' (action R). It then finds the latest earlier history entry with stage 'step-plan' and outcome 'done' for the same item (action P). It returns [] if either is missing, so first visits and other items are untouched. Otherwise it returns lines modelled on `_replan_delta_lines`: 'Revision {n} of {stage_spec.MAX_REVISES} for {item}: this item was sent back to step-plan.' 'The result that sent it back: {root}/results/{R}.md.' 'Your previous step plan: {root}/results/{P}.md. Amend it rather than write a new plan: keep every criterion, step, path and test command the evidence does not touch as written, with the same ids; change or add only what the evidence requires; say in the summary which rows are new or changed and which are carried over. Submit the whole amended plan; it replaces the previous one.' Avoid the verb 'revise' for the model's own action, since the Backchain guidance in the same packet uses 'repair/revise' for a different operation. Call it in `render` right after `lines.extend(_replan_delta_lines(root, state, stage))`, passing the `workitem` already computed there. No head change, no result-template change, no gate.

title: single source of truth: test-command home, pass-log conformance, result copies

design.summary: Three findings, three different answers. (1) Pass log: make the packet's pass-log line true by having the script check whether the log exists when it renders the packet (the `next` recovery command re-renders it), and drop the pass-log resource from the two Until Loop contracts, where the runtime receipt and handoff already own iteration state. (2) Test commands: drop enforcement and drop "point the docs at state.md"; document which source is authoritative for what. Four real runs (29 command rows) show no contradiction between docs and ledger, and a pointer into the run directory would break the committed, inherited knowledge home. (3) Result copies: drop. The inbox copy is a live recovery aid (a resumed model re-submitted its pre-kill result from it), and the results copy is equality-checked against state. Document the roles. Do not ship a blanket "start the log first" instruction yet. It would cost about one tool call per action, no run shows it would be followed, and the measured recoveries without a log cost almost nothing. That is an investigation with a stated question, not a build. Size: small, one patch note, no new state key, no compatibility path.
design.for_against:
PASS LOG (implement-smaller).
FOR the truthful pointer: the packet line (navigator._context_index_lines) says "open it first after a reset" whether or not the file exists. In the Grok 1230 run (events.jsonl, /Users/dadleet/e2e-runs/20261007/v1230-battleship-grok-none) 2 of the 2 reads of a pass log hit "does not exist" (event 10305 in test-green, 177 events after compaction 10128, just before the log was first written; event 14736 in the final stage, 68 events after compaction 14668). That run lost context 8 times (6 compactions at events 1722, 4314, 6693, 10128, 12067, 14668; 2 host cancellations at 11926 and 13415). The 1220 Grok run lost it 5 times (compactions at 1681, 4279, 6917, 8659, 10303). In all 13 cases no log existed for the action in progress. All 9 logs in 1230 were first written at 83 to 100 percent of their stage's events, 8 of 8 in 1220 within 2 to 18 events of the result write: closing summaries, not pass logs. 5 of 9 (1230) and 4 of 8 (1220) are cited in evidence_refs and so have a reader; the rest have none. Sonnet wrote none: 0 of 38 actions (v1230) and 0 of 46 (v1220), with no tool call touching notes/ in either events.jsonl. Making the line state what the script sees removes a false promise at the exact moment of recovery, costs no extra tool call, and keeps the aid. The present-file text stays byte-identical, so Grok's habit of closing notes that become evidence is untouched.
FOR dropping the loop-contract resource: test_loop.build_contract and quality.build_contract list the log as a resource ("append what each iteration checked and what is left"). The Until Loop runtime already requires a full compact `handoff` each iteration and re-serves it through next_argv (until_loop_ephemeral._active_packet), so the log is a second source for the same fact, and a frozen contract cannot say whether the file exists. In the 20 or so loop actions across the Grok runs, one had a log. The bytes saved are small: about 240 of 3.3 to 5.0 KB per real contract, 404 of the 9,216 budget in listing_problem's worst-case sizing, measured. So the reason is single source, not size.
AGAINST / unknown: 8 in-stage context losses in 1230 were all recovered from `next` plus the packet and scratch files; the only redone work was one rerun of `node restart-check.mjs` at event 13496 after a kill during 13412. That leans toward the aid being unnecessary, and retiring it is defensible. I did not choose it because the tenet and the earlier register decision keep recovery aids, and "would a mid-stage log have helped" is unmeasured, so it stays unknown, not zero. Shipping "start the log at the beginning of each pass" blind: Sonnet stages last at most 2.3 minutes (timeline.json, spec 2.3, no compaction signal), Grok's long stages are implement 14.5 and carry-forward 12.4 minutes, so a blanket instruction adds about 38 to 47 writes per run on the host that does not need them and benefits only the long small-window stages, which cannot be known in advance. Verdict: ship the truthful line and the contract change; hold the start nudge for a measured probe.
Rejected for the log: a script-created stub per action (47 abandoned stubs, worse for "written and abandoned"); refusing `complete` without a log (a recovery aid must never gate completion, the original rule from 95a4648d, and Sonnet would be refused 84 times); deleting the instruction (conflicts with the tenet while unmeasured).
TEST COMMANDS (drop enforcement; document). The competing prose home is real structurally: in the four runs, 29 distinct (kind, suite, command) ledger rows; 22 appear in at least one docs/shiploop file and 7 in none (all `check` one-liners, plus 2 per-item focused commands in v1220 Sonnet); the regression `node --test` appears in 6, 9, 8 and 9 prose files. No doc names a different test command than the ledger ran; the doc-only command strings are app-start commands and statements that a form fails (`node --test test/` as MODULE_NOT_FOUND). So there is no divergence to enforce against. The register's remedy, "docs point at state.md", fails twice: state.md lives in .shiploop-runs/<id>/run, not in the repository, while shiploop_knowledge_home commits docs/shiploop for later runs to inherit; and no run ever opens state.md (register: 0 opens), so it moves grounding into a record the model must find (SPEC S-6). The inverse, refusing a step plan whose regression command the strategy file does not list, would be a new refusal on every run for a gap that never hurt one; as a fenced-block check it would have refused both Sonnet runs, whose strategy files hold the command inline. KISS says document it. The truthful statement: the ledger's test_commands, system_commands and consumer_checks are what ShipLoop executes (test_loop.stage_commands); docs/shiploop/test-strategy.md is the repository's durable, inherited catalog of suite entry points; the per-item list is not repeated in docs; no script compares the two (known gap, measured).
RESULT COPIES (drop; document). inbox/<action>.md is retained for two real uses: replay (navigator._apply_result compares a repeated complete with accepted) and the pending draft. In 1230 the first `complete` (event 11923) was cancelled by the host kill at 11926; the resumed model re-read its inbox file (grep at 11973) and re-submitted (12001, exit 0). planning_context._live_run_dependency_reason already refuses the inbox as a planning dependency because it is mutable. results/<action>.md is the model-facing "Read first" copy, and planning_context.collect fails when its parsed content differs from state. The register said "byte-compares"; the code compares parsed records. state.md stays the one authority. The 240 KB of disk is not a defect.
TENET CHECK. Nothing leaves a packet: the pointer line is made true, the Recovery command and the loop receipt (next_argv) stay, and the inbox and results copies stay. The dropped contract resource was a pointer, not grounding. The SPEC S-6 probe condition (a clear-the-context probe inside a stage shows no redone work) is met for the contract change by the 1230 kills, which happened with no log present; a fresh probe after the build is listed under unknowns.

title: two evidence investigations: Sonnet cost rise and Grok Chrome about:blank

design.summary:
(1) SONNET COST RISE (20261006 v1220 vs 20261007 v1230, same prompt, same invocation.json apart from paths and local_head). Verdict: the model's own work, not packet growth. The engine text added between the two builds can explain at most about $0.06 of the $3.11 rise (about 2%).
Cost arithmetic. Rates of $2 input, $4 cache-write(1h), $0.20 cache-read and $10 output per million tokens reproduce both sessions' total_cost_usd exactly (6.5405192 and 9.6542784) from metrics.json sessions[0].usage; this is a fit, not a published price. Cache-read is 70.3% of the first run's cost and 73.7% of the second's. The $3.114 rise is cache-read +$2.519, cache-write +$0.262, output +$0.331. Model calls (unique assistant message ids) went 133 to 167; the harness's `turns` 238 to 294 counts content-block events (metrics.collect says so). Mean context per call went 174.8k to 215.0k tokens, so cache-read tokens rose 23.2M to 35.9M (+54.5%).
Why the rise is quadratic. The whole run is one un-cleared session, and every token added is re-read at every later call. Per-call context growth is almost equal (1,516 vs 1,602 tokens per call). Priced at equal length, the first 133 calls of the new run read 25.5M tokens (+9.7%), and its extra 34 calls (context 285k to 325k) read 10.4M, which is 82% of the increase.
Where it fell. I priced each call's context growth by how many later calls re-read it, per stage window from timeline.jsonl and state.md history. The growth term went $3.09 to $5.22 and the base term (calls times the 58.5k start context) $1.56 to $1.96. By stage: spec +$0.86 (calls 19 to 25; context added 40.2k to 60.6k tokens), plan +$0.32 (5 to 8; 7.9k to 18.8k), static-checks +$0.16 (5 to 12), intake +$0.13 (3 to 3 calls, same 16.7k to 17.2k content, only more later calls), implement +$0.12 (11 to 14), carry-forward +$0.07, get-next-work-item +$0.065, regression +$0.06.
What the extra work was.
- Spec: 4 Improve review passes vs 3; a Skill load of improve (+11.3k tokens); three Reads of the 46 KB nav-e05876...-improve.md (22.6k, 6.3k, 8.9k bytes); review-policy.md and ADAPTER.md read in full. The 2026-10-06 run read improve/SKILL.md once (29.5 KB) and used grep/sed windows of the packet.
- Plan: the model Read the plan packet in full (2.1k+14.5k bytes), read a backchain-planning section and an Outcomes rule, and ran backchain-check; the 2026-10-06 run used sed windows.
- static-checks: 3 quality-loop iterations vs 2, a 6.3 KB rubric read, two file Reads.
- Nine stages that took 1 call in the 2026-10-06 run took 17 calls in the 2026-10-07 run (verify, integrate, release-check, handoff, regression and others). The earlier model submitted blind; the later one read the packet or probed first.
- A test-green Until Loop done call was malformed once (error packet, two extra calls).
- The delivered product is larger: 26,030 to 34,983 bytes outside docs (+34%), docs +27%, a new test/page.test.js, and model-authored tool-input bytes +39% (165k to 230k). Work scale tracks the cost.
- The 2026-10-06 run was not a clean baseline: 46 accepted rows including one test-refine revise (the uncounted `node --test` refusal), then a cheap second pass of about 10 calls. The 2026-10-07 run had 38 rows and no revise, so first-pass calls rose 123 to 167 (+36%).
Packet-growth test.
- Engine diff (diff of the two build/plugins/skill-craft trees): shiploop_navigator._checked_line adds a 115 to 264 byte line to 45 packets (7,514 bytes in all). shiploop_prompts DUTIES add 660 bytes in three stages (test-strategy settle-facts, plan module-format, a reporter note). The case-end rule (CASE_END_STATES, commit 2cb2a9e4) is in neither build; it is 510 bytes in 5 stages, about $0.02 in future runs.
- Upper bound if every added byte entered context at its stage and was re-read at every later call: about $0.051 plus $0.007.
- Packet files for comparable stages grew +1.4% (25 producer-only stages, +10.3 KB) and +1.6% (8 Improve-reviewed stages, +5.2 KB), and part of that is model-authored text.
- Packet-bearing tool results excluding spec fell 99.5k to 84.9k bytes.
- The Checked by line reached the model in 28 tool results and was never quoted in a tool input or assistant text. Whether it changed behaviour is not excluded, but there is no sign of it.
- Same-build spread exists: baselines.jsonl hello 1.19.0 pair 194 to 254 turns ($5.37 to $7.33) on one build, although docs/shiploop-refusals-journal-2026-10-04.md attributes $1.44 of that $1.96 to one dead-end replan, so that spread is lumpy where this rise is broad.
- Design tension, not a defect proven: packet_head tells the model to Read the full packet with a file tool, and the packet files run 30 to 58 KB.
